messages.author: a3c668b849637905
messages.subject: dotplot point shapes
parts:
Hi,

I've not yet used geom_dotplot myself, this is pure curiosity.

Would it make sense to extend the grob and geom to accept other point
shapes? I imagine the shape should only vary between groups of points
(like fill/colour/alpha are presumably doing currently), not within
groups. We could then form Tetris-like shapes with little squares. Or
other less amusing things.

A slight technical difficulty comes from the fact that pointsGrob's
shapes vary in size
(http://tolstoy.newcastle.edu.au/R/e6/devel/09/05/1839.html), but this
could be accounted for with corresponding scaling factors.

Cheers,

b.

PS: I believe I raised this question in the past, but I forget where
and IIRC it wasn't followed up.

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: dotplot point shapes
parts:
Hi Baptiste -

The way it's written right now, it actually doesn't use pch points, since the relationship between their specified size and their actual size seems to be arbitrary and not consistent. I recall looking at some code you posted a while back where you used diamond shapes that had some scaling value to make them take up the desired amount of space. (That code was a great help, by the way!)

I ended up using circleGrob, because it allows precise control over the dimensions. If you look at grob-dotstack.r, you'll see where it uses circleGrob. I suppose it would be possible to implement other shapes and swap them in place of circleGrob. It might even be possible to have a scaling table and use pointsGrob, as you suggested. Is it common for dot plots to use shapes other than circles?

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: dotplot point shapes
parts:
Hi,

I had another look at the imaginative constants defining the point
shape sizes. As best as I could work out, the scaling factors for the
relevant shapes (fill and col) look like this,

fullSymbols <- function(type=c("round", "square", "diamond",
"utriangle", "dtriangle"),
size=unit(3, "cm"), ...){

type <- match.arg(type)
scaling <- switch(type,
"round" = 4/3,
"square" = 10 * par("cin")[1],
"diamond" = 10 * par("cin")[1] / sqrt(2),
"utriangle" = 1,
"dtriangle" = 1)

pch <- switch(type,
"round" = 21,
"square" = 22,
"diamond" = 23,
"utriangle" = 24,
"dtriangle" = 25)

g <- pointsGrob(pch=pch, size=scaling*size, default.units="npc",
gp=gpar(col="red", fill="blue", alpha=0.5, lwd=20),
x=0.5,y=0.5,...)
b <- rectGrob(x=0.5,y=0.5, width=size, height=size,
gp=gpar(lty=2, fill=NA, col="black")) # snug box to size

gTree(children=gList(g, b))
}

grid.newpage()
library(gridExtra)
grid.arrange(
fullSymbols("round"),
fullSymbols("square"),
fullSymbols("diamond"),
fullSymbols("utriangle"),
fullSymbols("dtriangle"))

and the last two presumably require some offset as well.

I don't know if it's useful, but if people have started mapping
colour, then I'm guessing shape might be desirable too (if only for
black and white prints).

Cheers,

b.

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: dotplot point shapes
parts:
I think the idea is to fit them into the bounding box. It's critical that they all have the same width, because dot width represents bin width. Also, it's important that they each have the same height, so that for any number of dots, they stack to the same height (useful for comparing groups).

I think the square doesn't work, since the stacked points would be indistinguishable. The triangles should be usable. They don't have to fit exactly into the bounding box. If they're a little smaller, I think that's OK. The triangles would look a little strange when stacking along the x axis instead of y. It would probably be a good idea to rotate them in that case.

Baptiste - thanks for figuring out the scaling ratios!

-Winston
